body.statement:
Let \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), and \(d\in\{A,B\}\).  The raw design-A fiber has a polynomial presentation with
\[
 N_A=4\ell+8k,\qquad
 S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4,\qquad
 D_A=2,
\]
and the raw design-B fiber has one with
\[
 N_B=4\ell+9k+8,\qquad
 S_B=4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15,\qquad
 D_B=3.
\]
The unequal-target refinement adds one sign atom and does not increase \(D_d\).  Define
\[
 (A_{S,d},D_{S,d})=\mathsf{Samp}(N_d,S_d,D_d),
 \qquad
 (A_{E,d},D_{E,d})=\mathsf{Exist}(N_d,S_d+1,D_d),
\]
where the published bounds are coordinatewise nondecreasing, and put
\[
 R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_d=\max\{D_{S,d},D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\},
 \qquad
 R_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}R_d,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}\mathcal D_d.
\]
Then the mandatory compiler terminates after at most one raw-fiber sampling call and, if that fiber is nonempty, one unequal-target existential call.  Its record/output count is at most \(R_{k,\ell}\).  Every coordinate of the initial sample has algebraic degree at most \(D_{S,d}\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); every coordinate of a second-stage witness has degree at most \(D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\) over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); and every returned coordinate consequently has degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\).  No assertion is made that the initial sample lies in the field generated by the second-stage witness and its target.

The separate diagnostic structural enumerations have at most
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4
\]
templates.  These counts do not multiply \(R_{k,\ell}\), and their auxiliary chart variables do not enter \(N_d,S_d,D_d\).

If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\), there is a universal constant \(C\ge1\), independent of \(k,\ell\) and the input, such that
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\le 2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}\le 2^{CQ^C}.
\]
Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.

For rational input coordinates whose numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\), let
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
 \qquad
 c_k=1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil,
 \qquad
 h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0),
\]
and define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{E,d}
 &=\mathsf{Exist}_h
   (N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d}+c_k,D_{S,d}),\\
 h_{F,0,d}
 &=\mathsf{Flat}_h(D_{S,d},h_{S,d}+c_k+1),\\
 h_{F,1,d}
 &=\mathsf{Flat}_h
   (D_{S,d}D_{E,d},h_{S,d}+c_k+h_{E,d}+1),\\
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 &=\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}
   \{h_{S,d},h_{E,d},h_{F,0,d},h_{F,1,d}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
After flattening separately when necessary and clearing only guarded observable denominators, every initial-sample, target, or second-stage witness coordinate can be represented by a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(\mathcal D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.
\]
Thus record/output count and algebraic degree have singly exponential fixed-alphabet bounds, whereas rational height obeys the separate displayed bound.  A rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  Connected-component description, target projection, diagnostic-chart iteration, and a generic two-copy classifier are not required decision stages.
body.justification: The theorem bounds the actual two-call raw-fiber engine, treats the initial sample and second-stage witness in their correct algebraic fields, and charges the target-coordinate sum height before the existential call.
body.gap: Chart counts belong to optional diagnostics, while the initial sample need not lie in the field generated by the sampled target and the second-stage witness.
body.consumer: Exact implementations receive raw degree two for design A, raw degree three for design B, no chart multiplier, separate initial and second-stage degree bounds, and a rational-height recurrence containing the target-sum increment.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\in\{A,B\}\).  We first count a direct polynomial presentation of the raw fiber.  In design A, the four endpoint vectors \(b_i\) contribute \(4\ell\) variables and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells contribute \(8k\), giving
\[
 N_A=4\ell+8k.                                             \tag{27}
\]
Endpoint nonnegativity and the four endpoint normalizations use \(4\ell+4\) atoms.  Coefficient nonnegativity uses \(8k\), the four equations \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\) use \(4k\), and the factorization equations use \(4k\ell\).  Thus
\[
 S_A=4k\ell+4\ell+12k+4.                                 \tag{28}
\]
Factorization is bilinear in \((b,a)\), and every other design-A atom is linear, so \(D_A=2\).

The raw design-B presentation adds four coordinates for \(m\), \(k\) for \(g\), and four for \(\pi\).  Hence
\[
 N_B=N_A+4+k+4=4\ell+9k+8.                               \tag{29}
\]
Margin positivity and normalization add five atoms, common-instrument positivity and normalization add \(k+1\), response-mass nonnegativity and normalization add five, and the response-level shared-\(Z\) equations add \(4k\).  Relevance is the finite disjunction of the two strict signs of
\[
 q^X_zg(z')-q^X_{z'}g(z)                                  \tag{30}
\]
over unordered \(\{z,z'\}\).  Counting both ordered signs conservatively by \(2k(k-1)\) and adding these terms to (28) gives
\[
 S_B\le 4k\ell+2k^2+4\ell+15k+15.                        \tag{31}
\]
The shared-\(Z\) equations have degree two because they contain \(m_ea_{ei}(z)\) and \(\pi_i g(z)\).  Since \(q^X_z\) is bilinear in \((m,a)\), (30) has degree three.  Thus \(D_B=3\).  The target is linear, so its squared-distance inequality adds one sign atom of degree two and does not enlarge \(D_d\).

Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\) once to the raw design-\(d\) fiber over \(K=\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  It generates at most \(A_{S,d}\) records.  When the fiber is nonempty, let \(\xi\) be the primitive element in the real-univariate representation of \(x_0\).  The sampling degree bound gives
\[
 [K(\xi):K]\le D_{S,d}.                                  \tag{32}
\]
Every coordinate of \(x_0\) lies in \(K(\xi)\), so its degree over \(K\) is at most \(D_{S,d}\).  The two coordinates of \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) are linear sums of coordinates of \(x_0\); hence
\[
 K(t_0)\subseteq K(\xi),
 \qquad [K(t_0):K]\le D_{S,d}.                           \tag{33}
\]

There is one existential-realizability call over \(K(t_0)\) on the raw fiber plus the squared-distance sign condition.  It generates at most \(A_{E,d}\) records.  If it returns a witness with primitive element \(\upsilon\), then
\[
 [K(t_0,\upsilon):K(t_0)]\le D_{E,d}.                    \tag{34}
\]
Multiplicativity of finite extension degrees, (33), and (34) imply
\[
 [K(t_0,\upsilon):K]
 =[K(t_0,\upsilon):K(t_0)][K(t_0):K]
 \le D_{S,d}D_{E,d}.                                     \tag{35}
\]
Each second-stage witness coordinate lies in \(K(t_0,\upsilon)\), and therefore has degree at most the right side of (35).  The initial coordinates were bounded separately in (32); in general they need not lie in \(K(t_0,\upsilon)\).  Taking
\[
 \mathcal D_d=\max\{D_{S,d},D_{S,d}D_{E,d}\}             \tag{36}
\]
therefore bounds every returned coordinate without making a false field-containment assertion.  The tower-flattening, square-free-factorization, Thom-sign, and isolation procedures in the cited lemma do not increase field degree.  The two fixed status/output records and the two algorithmic record bounds give
\[
 R_d=2+A_{S,d}+A_{E,d}.                                   \tag{37}
\]
There is no chart multiplier because both calls use the single raw fiber.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) separately gives the optional diagnostic counts
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4.                                  \tag{38}
\]
The list (38) terminates when requested, but it occurs in neither (27)--(31) nor (36)--(37).

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\).  Equations (27)--(31) yield, after increasing a universal constant \(C\),
\[
 N_d\le CQ,\qquad S_d\le CQ,\qquad D_d\le3.             \tag{39}
\]
The coordinatewise nondecreasing bounds in the effective-semialgebraic lemma then give
\[
 A_{S,d},D_{S,d},A_{E,d},D_{E,d}
 \le 2^{CQ^C}.                                             \tag{40}
\]
Substitution in (36)--(37), and enlargement of \(C\) once more, proves
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\le2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_{k,\ell}\le2^{CQ^C}.                        \tag{41}
\]
Selected-table positivity gives \(r_e>0\), so the only observable divisions used to form \(T_e\) and \(v_e\) are guarded.  All raw coefficients consequently lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Effective field arithmetic, order, sign determination, sampling, and real-root procedures from the cited lemma terminate, proving relative termination over an arbitrary real input field.

Now suppose the input coordinates are rational with numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing the deleted simplex coordinates, forming \(r_e\), dividing to obtain \(T_e,v_e\), and clearing the nonzero observable denominators in degree-at-most-three polynomials requires only a quadratic number of rational additions and multiplications in \(Q\).  Therefore
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1)                                            \tag{42}
\]
conservatively bounds every cleared integer coefficient.  The sampling height bound is
\[
 h_{S,d}=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_d,S_d,D_d,h_0).                 \tag{43}
\]
Each coordinate of \(t_0\) is a sum of at most \(k\) coordinates represented in the initial real-univariate representation.  Adding at most \(k\) integer numerators increases binary length by at most
\(c_k=1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\); consequently \(t_0\) has representation height at most \(h_{S,d}+c_k\).  The correct relative second-stage bound is therefore
\[
 h_{E,d}=\mathsf{Exist}_h
 (N_d,S_d+1,D_d;h_0,h_{S,d}+c_k,D_{S,d}).                  \tag{44}
\]

The initial representation and the second-stage tower must also be normalized separately.  Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{F,0,d}
 &=\mathsf{Flat}_h(D_{S,d},h_{S,d}+c_k+1),\\
 h_{F,1,d}
 &=\mathsf{Flat}_h
   (D_{S,d}D_{E,d},h_{S,d}+c_k+h_{E,d}+1).
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{45}
\]
The first line covers \(x_0\) and its coordinate sums; the second covers the field \(K(t_0,\upsilon)\) and explicitly retains the increment \(c_k\).  Thus
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 =\max_{d\in\{A,B\}}
   \{h_{S,d},h_{E,d},h_{F,0,d},h_{F,1,d}\}               \tag{46}
\]
bounds the coefficient and rational-isolation lengths of every output.  The height envelopes in the cited lemma, (39), and (40), after a final enlargement of \(C\), imply
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}.                  \tag{47}
\]
This is a separate rational-height guarantee, not a claim that height is singly exponential in the same sense as the record and degree bounds (41).  The rational square-free and isolation subroutines are finite, so a rational-input Turing implementation terminates.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}rigidity\text{-}atlas}\) proves that the two raw-fiber calls decide the causal target; connected components, target projection, chart iteration, and a generic two-copy classifier are unnecessary.
